place.en: Mount Chending · The clifftop behind the temple

setup.zh: 八月里，瞿老叫你上崖顶。他瞧你一眼：「九层，满了。」你伸出九根指头——攥了五年的掌心也张开了。
setup.en: In the eighth month Old Qu calls you up the cliff. One glance: "Layer nine — and full." You hold up nine fingers, and the palm you've kept clenched five years opens too.

recap.zh: 瞿老讲了他四十多年前最后一个徒弟：宗门大比头名，吃了观里那颗一转的丹，退了三层，下山教娃娃算账——那是你外公。「那颗丹，别吃。」
recap.en: Old Qu told of his last disciple, more than forty years ago: first at the whole-temple contest, he ate the temple's one-turn pill, fell back three layers, and went down the mountain to teach children sums — your grandfather. "That pill — don't eat it."

zh: 九根指头。掌心一个圈，圈里一横。
en: Nine fingers. In the palm, a circle with a bar across it.

story.zh:
太阳落了山，瞿老瞧了他一眼，道：「九层，满了。」小满点点头，伸出九根指头给师父看。

九根指头一张开，那只在人前攥了五年的掌心，便也张开了。瞿老的眼睛没在他的指头上，落在他掌心里：一个圈，圈里一横，颜色比旁的皮肉深一层，像烙进去的，又像是从里头长出来的。腊八那天镜光打在上头，烙下来，五年里他吃了六七十颗九纹的聚气丹，伤好了，皮也换了，它一点也没褪。

瞿老伸手，把他那只手翻过来，又翻过去，看了一会儿，从自己袍子下摆撕下一条布，一圈一圈，给他缠上了，缠得极紧，末了打了个死结，道：「这东西，别给人看。」

瞿老没有笑。他看着崖下那一片云，看了很久，才道：「用哪颗丹？」

小满心里「咯噔」一下，嘴上却答得极快：「观里那颗。」

瞿老道：「坐下。」
story.en:
When the sun had set, Old Qu glanced at him and said: "Layer nine — and full." Xiaoman nodded and held up nine fingers for his master to see.

With nine fingers spread, the palm he had kept clenched in front of people for five years opened too. Old Qu's eyes were not on his fingers but in his palm: a circle with one stroke across it, a shade darker than the skin around it, as if burned in — or as if grown from inside. The mirror's light had struck it on the day of Laba and branded it there; in five years he had eaten sixty or seventy nine-ring qi pills, the hurts had healed, the skin had renewed itself, and it had not faded at all.

Old Qu took his hand, turned it over, and back, looked a while, tore a strip from the hem of his own robe and wound it round, turn after turn, very tight, and tied it off in a hard knot: "That thing — let no one see it."

Old Qu did not smile. He looked at the clouds below the cliff for a long time before he said: "Which pill will you use?"

Xiaoman's heart gave a jolt, but his mouth answered very fast: "The temple's."

Old Qu said: "Sit down."

label.en: Sit, and listen to your master

exits.means: sits and listens to his master's story of his last disciple

story.zh:
瞿老道：「四十多年前，我收过一个徒弟。」

「他是徐州人，跟你一样。家里穷，跟你一样。进山门的时候，爬石阶，爬到一百六十级，腿动不了了，坐在那里喘，喘了一炷香，又站起来接着爬——那一年，只有他一个坐下了又站起来的。我在第三百级上瞧见了，就记住了他。我跟他说的头一句话，是『涧上那块石头，滑』。」

「第七年上，他九层大圆满了，捧着那只玉盒子来问我，吃不吃。」瞿老道，「我说，吃。」

「他冲了一夜。天亮的时候，我进屋去看他，他坐在那里，满脸是黑斑，丹田里那股气，散了一半。丹毒淤在经脉里，退了三层，再也冲不上去了。」

「他走的时候，只带了一身旧袍子，和他自己抄的《河洛剑诀》开篇三页——竹简留在观里，他一笔一笔抄在纸上带走的。他说，剑是练不成了，那九个数，好看，拿去教娃娃算账，横也十五，竖也十五，娃娃们喜欢。」

小满这时候，已经什么都明白了。

那本书，原来不是书。是外公自己抄的三页纸，是一门剑，是一个人没走完的一步。

「那颗丹，别吃。」

「凭你自己冲。」瞿老道，「没丹，冲得过的少。可没丹，也没毒——冲不过，身子记下这一回，下一回多一分。冲到老也冲不过，不过是这辈子停在练气——停在练气，也能活。也能回家，教娃娃算账。」

那天夜里，小满在草屋里睁着眼躺着。木牌里那个声音，许久没有自己开过口了，这时候却开了：「那老头说得对，也不对。」

隔了一会儿，又道：「一转的丹，炉里只转了一回；那几点黑，是没炼干净的渣。炉里少转的几转，拿身子补上。」

「头一样，化。别一口吞，压在舌头底下，让它一层一层地化，药力一丝一丝地进。第二样，炼。进一丝，推一个周天，药力留下，渣子推到皮上，出一身黑汗，臭的。推一回，就是一转——几天的事，不是一夜。第三样，等。汗出清了，药力坐稳了，再冲关；别挑它最冲的时候冲。」

她打了个哈欠：「跟你在秘境里吸灵气一个理，一口一口来。」便再没有声音了。

小满躺在那里，想起外公那一夜：一颗一转的丹，一口吞下去，当夜就冲，药力和毒，一齐撞在那一道关上。
story.en:
Old Qu said: "More than forty years ago, I took a disciple."

"He was from Xu, like you. His family was poor, like yours. When he came to the gate he climbed the steps, and at the hundred and sixtieth his legs gave out; he sat there panting for the time of an incense stick, then got up and climbed on — that year he was the only one who sat down and got up again. I saw it from the three hundredth step, and I remembered him. The first thing I ever said to him was: 'The stone over the gully is slippery.'"

"In the seventh year he reached layer nine, great perfection, and came holding that jade box to ask me whether to eat it." Old Qu said, "I said: eat."

"He pushed all night. At daybreak I went in to see him. He was sitting there, his face covered in dark flecks, the qi in his dantian half scattered. The pill's poison had clotted in his channels; he fell back three layers and never broke through again."

"When he left he took only an old robe and the first three pages of the He-Luo Sword Art, copied in his own hand — the bamboo slips stayed in the temple; he copied them onto paper stroke by stroke and took that. He said the sword was beyond him now, but the nine numbers were pretty — he'd use them to teach children sums: fifteen across, fifteen down; children like that."

By now Xiaoman understood everything.

That book had never been a book. It was three pages Grandfather had copied himself, a sword art, and one step a man never finished.

"That pill — don't eat it."

"Push through on your own," Old Qu said. "Without a pill, few make it. But without a pill there's no poison either — fail, and the body remembers the time, and the next time it has a little more. Fail till you're old, and you stay in Qi Condensation for life — and in Qi Condensation you can still live. You can still go home and teach children sums."

That night Xiaoman lay awake in the thatched hut. The voice in the token had not spoken of its own accord for a long time; now it did: "The old man is right, and he is wrong."

After a while: "A one-turn pill has been turned in the furnace once; those black specks are the dregs it didn't refine away. The turns the furnace left out, the body makes up."

"First, melt it. Don't gulp it down; keep it under your tongue and let it melt layer by layer, so the drug comes in one thread at a time. Second, refine. One thread in, one full circuit; the drug's strength stays, the dregs are pushed out to the skin and leave as a black sweat, foul-smelling. Each round is one more turn — days of work, not one night. Third, wait. When the sweat runs clear and the strength sits steady, then charge the barrier; not when it surges highest."

She yawned. "Same as drawing qi in the hidden realm: a mouthful at a time." And then there was no more sound.

Xiaoman lay there and thought of Grandfather's night: a one-turn pill swallowed in one gulp, the barrier charged that same night, the drug and the poison crashing into it together.

exits.means: asks his master the disciple's name, or about the old invitation

text.zh: 瞿老把一张发黄的拜师帖在青石上展开。名字那一格，给雨水洇成了一团，一个字也认不出来了。他道：「杜子安。他叫杜子安。」
text.en: Old Qu unfolds a yellowed invitation card on the bluestone. The name box has been blotted by rain into one smudge; not a character can be read. He says: "Du Zi'an. His name was Du Zi'an."
